title: A series of tetranuclear rare-earth complexes and two-step slow magnetic relaxation in Dy4 complex

synthesis.procedure: Triethylamine (0.0152 g, 0.15 mmol) was added to a MeCN (10 mL) solution of Tb(NO3)3·6H2O (0.1 mmol) and H3L (0.0456 g, 0.1 mmol) at room temperature. After stirring for 0.5 h, the mixture was transferred to a 15 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 100 °C for 5 days, then cooled to 30 °C at 5 °C every 2 h. Yellow block crystals were collected and washed 3–5 times with cold MeOH.
synthesis.temperature: stirring at room temperature, then solvothermal heating at 100 °C; cooled to 30 °C
synthesis.time: stir 0.5 h; heat 5 days; cool at 5 °C every 2 h
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 15 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, solvothermal, precision thermostatic blast oven
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow block-shaped crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction were collected and washed 3–5 times with cold MeOH.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility of polycrystalline 1 under 0.1 T shows χMT = 42.97 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (below 47.28 cm3 K mol−1 for four uncoupled TbIII), decreasing to 23.30 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, attributed to antiferromagnetic interactions and thermal depopulation of Stark sublevels. Magnetization at 2.0 K reaches 17.81 Nβ at 70 kOe, well below the 36 Nβ saturation estimate, indicating magnetic anisotropy and/or low-lying excited states. No SMM energy-barrier analysis is reported for 1.

properties.summary: Complex 2 is a Dy4 SMM with two-step slow magnetic relaxation. Room-temperature χMT is 52.40 cm3 K mol−1 (vs 56.68 cm3 K mol−1 for four uncoupled DyIII). χMT falls to 47.52 cm3 K mol−1 at 16 K then rises to 54.09 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with ferromagnetic DyIII–DyIII coupling competing with Stark depopulation. Magnetization at 2.0 K reaches 19.15 Nβ at 70 kOe (below ~40 Nβ). Zero-dc-field ac data (2.0 Oe oscillation) show frequency-dependent χ′ and χ″ with χ″ peaks at 2–4 K and 5–11 K. Arrhenius fits give Ueff = 20.98 K (τ0 = 7.66×10−7 s) and 43.47 K (τ0 = 9.75×10−7 s). Cole–Cole α = 0.048–0.16.
